Replace every one of the four views with a real photograph of the real-world object this model stands for: a medieval weaver's shop: cream plaster walls in a dark oak half-timber frame, steep blue tile gable roof, cream stone chimney with square cap at the back, blue banner with white crossed-thread emblem on the gable, dark oak plank door in a rounded stone archway with stone steps, blue-and-white striped awning over the doorway, spinning wheel with thread spools on a table at the left, wooden loom with blue-and-white cloth in front, two oak barrels of cloth at the right, iron lantern by the door, green conifer and oak fence at the back right. This is not a 3D render, not a game asset, not a toy, figurine or miniature, not clay or plastic, not a painting or an illustration and not a cartoon: it is a real object photographed in the real world. Keep exactly the same design as <image1>: the same parts in the same places, the same colour scheme, the same pose, and in each of the four views the same camera angle and the same side of the object. Each photograph shows the whole object, centred, cut out on a plain flat light grey background, with no ground beneath it, no base, platform or patch of grass, no shadow on the ground, no text, no labels and no lines or frames between the four views.
